title: Module manager: layout and external modules
objective: Let a person turn built-in modules off and on and reorder the tools panel and mode strip (phase 1), then install separately authored adjustment modules that run as sandboxed WebAssembly with their own WGSL programs, from a package file (phase 2).
context_summary: Owner decisions of 2026-10-25 are in docs/decisions.md and docs/design/module-manager.md: phase 1 arranges the panel and the mode strip; external modules are WASM plus WGSL; the first kind is an adjustment section; there is no community index yet. The layout is a presentation-only preference that never changes the registry order, rendering or schema.list; an off module stays registered so its photos render and export. An external module is a field-patch module from its manifest whose colour unit runs in WebAssembly with no imports; installs apply at the next launch. Phase 1 (TASK-001 to TASK-004) and phase 2 (TASK-005 to TASK-012) start independently. Routine engineering, layout and numerical choices are delegated within the design. The owner authorized implementation. Minimum model: the high tier; re-review against current main before each task.

tasks.description: Core module layout: the descriptor's toolset and locked fields, placements derived in the core, the person's module_layout in preferences.json, module.layout.read, module.enable, module.disable, module.order.set and module.layout.reset, the new module.list fields and the module.layout event.
extra_context: Add `toolset` (required; one of adjustments, corrections, masking, tools, processing) and `locked` (optional {reason}) to ModuleDescriptor in crates/luxforge-core/src/modules/descriptor/types.rs. Every built-in declares its home as the design lists; Crop, transform, straighten, Basic and RAW declare locked. Regenerate the built-in descriptor snapshot and the MCP static schema the snapshot tests pin.

Derive placements in the core from existing declarations, moving the desktop's rule unchanged: a drawn section (state/tools.rs draws_section), a crop-frame or brush-mask takeover canvas (state/canvas.rs's strip derivation, state/corrections.rs brush_module), a fill- task or object pick (state/remove.rs, object_pick.rs) and object selection. module.list answers toolset, locked, origin (built-in for every linked module), placements and the person's enabled.

Store `module_layout {disabled: [id], order: {adjustments: [id], tools: [id]}}` in Preferences (crates/luxforge-core/src/preferences.rs) through the existing bounded, locked, format-marked writer. It is written only by the module.* layout methods, never by preferences.set, as usage_statistics is. Only explicit choices are stored; unregistered ids are kept and listed as unrecognized; a newly registered module takes its default place after its preceding registry neighbour. Implementation of that merge is delegated within this rule.

Do not touch ModuleRegistry::assemble or the registry order: providers() order decides Original layers, first-open, the GPU warm list and the Corrections/Remove/Object providers. The layout is presentation only and never consulted by rendering, planning or presets.

Methods go in crates/luxforge-core/src/api/methods.rs beside module.list. Locked and unregistered ids refuse with invalid-params by name; module.order.set refuses anything but a permutation of that toolset's registered placements. Each change answers the new layout and announces module.layout. Evidence runs keep the layout inside their evidence directory.

tasks.description: Desktop workspace follows the layout: the tools panel in the person's order with the band context menu and the off-modules footer, the mode strip's order and its ⋯ menu, the palette and keymap without off modules, letter precedence, and the Off · edit kept band.
extra_context: Read module.layout.read with module.list in app/tasks.rs's modules task and again on the module.layout event in app/sync.rs. Derive the effective layout once in state/ and feed tools::derive (state/tools.rs), the strip (state/canvas.rs), palette::derive (state/palette.rs), mode_shortcuts and action_shortcuts (state/tools.rs, state/host_commands.rs) and app/keymap.rs from it. No layout logic in widgets.
Placements now come from module.list; remove the desktop's own copy of the rule moved into the core.

The Off · edit kept band: a module that is off but has a non-neutral layer in the displayed recipe (the recipe.describe row the band's dot already reads) draws at its place, collapsed, in the neutral grey, listing its values read-only with Enable Title. It differs from the delivered unavailable band, which stays red.
Letter precedence: host letters first, then registry order; a later claimant gets no letter and its tooltip names the owner. Today's built-ins do not collide, so test it with a variant registry.
Board B, C and D in the design's board are the visual reference; layout details are delegated to the implementer within the module-panel density and hierarchy.

tasks.description: External module contract: the luxforge-module.toml manifest, the .lfmodule package and its bounded reader and validator in the core, the luxforge:module/adjustment@0.1 WIT world, and the manifest's field table turned into a field-patch Spec.
extra_context: The core reads and validates packages without any WebAssembly engine: zip size and entry limits, no paths outside the root, manifest fields as the design lists, an id that is reverse-DNS, not luxforge.*, and a valid identity, toolset adjustments only, one effect on the colour or finish stage, not maskable, every source kind.

Field tables use the existing parameter and control vocabulary. Build them through field_patch.rs's Spec so the host's checks refuse a table it could not draw; Spec currently takes static data and may need owned strings, a delegated change that must leave built-ins' descriptors byte-identical.
The WIT world exports coefficients, apply-row and label, and declares no imports. Put the .wit file where both the host crate and the SDK read it (a delegated location).
Independent of phase 1; it can start now.

tasks.description: The luxforge-wasm crate: a pinned Wasmtime host that instantiates an adjustment component with no imports, bounded memory, epoch deadlines, deterministic floats and a compiled-code cache, and provides a ToolModule per package to the one registry assembly.
extra_context: Pin Wasmtime with the component model; relaxed SIMD and threads off, NaN canonicalization on; keep notices; no licence audit is claimed. Record binary-size and build-time deltas in the hand-off.

A provider is a field-patch module from TASK-005's Spec whose FieldPatch::compile calls coefficients and returns a PointwiseColor whose apply_row calls apply-row on a per-worker instance created lazily; identity is the words. A trap, deadline or wrong-length answer fails the render with an error naming the module and never a partial frame.

Extend RegistryOptions with the external providers so ModuleRegistry::assemble stays the one assembly (the registry-assembly repository rule); externals register after the built-ins, so registry-order roles are unaffected. A package that fails to instantiate registers unavailable with its reason via the existing path.
luxforge-core names neither Wasmtime nor a GPU crate; the desktop and luxforge-json link luxforge-wasm.
Answer the performance-rules checklist in the hand-off; measurement is TASK-012's.

tasks.description: External GPU programs: load program.wgsl as a Colour program at runtime, validate it with naga under the surface prelude, give its names a unique prefix, and enable it only after a bounded first-use probe against the reference within the colour class's tolerance, cached per package hash and adapter.
extra_context: GpuProgram holds &'static text and GPU_PROGRAMS is a static list; let runtime programs join the surface's and tile worker's program sets for the launch (a delegated representation: leaked per-launch strings or a shared owned type), without a GPU dependency in the core.

Names must start with lf_module; the loader rewrites the prefix to a unique one after a naga parse, not by text search. A program that fails validation is not registered and the module renders through the reference with the program named.

The probe renders fixed probe patches at field values spanning each range through the reference and the GPU on a worker at first use, never at launch, and sets the program enabled within the colour class's limits; otherwise GpuFallback::DisabledProgram names it. Cache the result under the data root.

tasks.description: Install store and lifecycle API: modules.json and the per-version store under the data root, module.package.inspect, module.install, module.uninstall, module.folder.load and module.folder.remove in developer mode, load states in module.status, the module.installed event, and assembly of installed modules in the desktop and luxforge-json at launch.
extra_context: Every write takes effect at the next launch; module.status reports pending-relaunch until then. A same-id install replaces at relaunch and its answer says when the payload format differs from the installed one. No rollback store.
